name: evn-alpha-micropython
description: Early-access tooling for the EVN ALPHA robotics controller: flash the MicroPython firmware, run programs, open the REPL, autocomplete for the evn motor API, and a Blockly block editor that generates MicroPython.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: The extension reads its own files and the programs you open; the board is reached over a port you choose.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Your programs can live in a virtual folder (the browser's projects folder); flashing the firmware needs the desktop.

evn.port.description: Which board to use. The USB serial number of an EVN ALPHA (for example E46320165B5F2A36) — the board is then found again whatever COM number Windows gives it — or a port name such as COM7 or /dev/ttyACM0, which is what a Bluetooth port needs. "EVN: Choose the board port" stores the serial number for an EVN ALPHA. Leave empty to auto-detect the EVN ALPHA (USB 2e8a:000a).

evn.pythonPath.description: Python interpreter used to run mpremote. Leave empty to use the Python extension's selected interpreter, then `py -3` / `python3` / `python` from PATH.

evn.replAfterRun.description: After running a file, stay connected in the REPL so the program's output stays visible and the board can be inspected (Ctrl+] leaves the REPL).

evn.blocks.renderer.description: Look of the blocks in the block editor: zelos (rounded, Scratch-like), geras (classic Blockly), thrasos (classic, updated). Takes effect when a blocks file is (re)opened.

evn.blocks.showCode.description: Show the generated MicroPython next to the blocks. The pane's minimise button collapses it to a Python pill on the block canvas; the pill brings it back.

evn.blocks.theme.description: Colour scheme of the block editor: auto follows the VS Code colour theme; light and dark force one (the scheme button in the block editor cycles through them).

evn.projectsFolder.description: Folder that holds your EVN programs (.py and .evnblocks), shown in the EVN ALPHA sidebar under "My projects". Leave empty for "EVN Projects" in your Documents folder (or in your home folder when there is no Documents). It is created when the extension starts.

enumDescriptions: Show evn documentation on hover only where no Pylance / Pyright / BasedPyright shows it: the browser IDE, Jedi, no Python extension, examples opened from the Examples view, and files the evn stubs do not reach
Always show the extension's evn hover, also next to the language server's
Never: hovers come from the language server only
evn.python.hover.description: Hover documentation for the evn module in Python files, from the extension's own copy of the stubs (typings/evn.pyi).

evn.docsUrl.description: Web address of the online documentation. The Documentation button opens it; "Open online documentation for the symbol under the cursor" opens it at the matching section of the API reference. The update check reads latest.json from it and installs only a VSIX published there, so it is a user setting only (a folder's settings cannot change it).

evn.updates.check.description: Once a day, look up whether a newer extension or firmware has been published (one small download of latest.json from the documentation site; nothing is installed without asking).

evn.console.enabled.description: Keep a live link to the board whenever no program is running and the REPL is closed: motor angles, battery, the devices on the I2C ports and a command line in the Board section. The link is dropped while a program runs and never interrupts a program the board started by itself from main.py.

enumDescriptions: 4 updates a second, the same as USB
evn.console.bluetoothRate.description: Live console: telemetry updates a second over Bluetooth (USB always uses 4). Fewer updates leave more air time for your own program's Bluetooth traffic.

evn.battery.warnVolts.description: Show a battery warning in the status bar when the pack drops below this voltage while the live console is connected. The EVN ALPHA pack is two cells, so 7.0 V is 3.5 V a cell. 0 turns the warning off.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with the EVN ALPHA
walkthroughs.description: Install the one tool the extension needs, flash the firmware, run an example, then write your own program.

steps.title: Install mpremote
steps.description:
The extension talks to the board with mpremote, a small Python tool. This step needs Python 3 on your computer.
[Install mpremote](command:evn.installMpremote)

steps.title: Choose the board port
steps.description:
In a browser there is nothing to install: the board is reached over Web Serial. Plug it in and let this page use the port - the browser asks you which device, and remembers it.
[Choose the board port](command:evn.selectPort)

steps.title: Flash the firmware
steps.description:
Put the EVN ALPHA MicroPython firmware on the board. Once, and again whenever the extension bundles a newer one.
[Flash the firmware](command:evn.flashFirmware)

steps.title: Run an example
steps.description:
Pick an example in the Examples section of the EVN ALPHA sidebar and press its Run button. Keep the wheels off the ground.
[Show the examples](command:evn.examples.focus)

steps.title: Write your own program
steps.description:
Create a Python or blocks program. It is saved in your projects folder and runs with Ctrl+F5.
[New Python program](command:evn.newPythonProject)
[New blocks program](command:evn.newBlocksProject)
Want autocomplete for evn in every Python file, not only inside your projects folder? [Turn it on](command:evn.enableGlobalAutocomplete)

steps.title: Learn more
steps.description:
The online documentation covers every motor call, the board, the sensors and the blocks.
[Open the documentation](command:evn.openDocumentation)
